body:
Disposable vapes are sold fully charged and pre-filled, which makes them the easiest way into vaping for adults: there is nothing to fill, no coil to change and nothing to learn. They are also the category with the widest spread in quality, size and price, and our catalog alone lists more than 1,100 of them. A few minutes of checking before you buy makes a big difference to value and to how much you enjoy the device. This guide walks through seven things to check in order, explains how to turn the numbers on the box into a fair comparison, gives worked examples, covers storage, charging and disposal, and ends with a short list of mistakes to avoid. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and nothing here is medical advice.

## 1. Puff count versus how you vape
Puff counts on the box are manufacturer estimates. A 5,000-puff device and a 30,000-puff device can both feel the same in your hand, but the larger one holds more liquid and usually carries a bigger battery. If you vape occasionally, a smaller device means less commitment and less waste, because you will not be stuck with a flavor you tire of. If you vape daily, a larger device usually costs much less per puff. Be honest about how much you use: a device that is too large for your use may go stale or lose battery life before you finish it, and one that is too small means frequent repurchases. See [puff counts explained](/blog/puff-count-explained/) for how the number is estimated and why real results differ.

### A quick way to estimate your own use
If you take about 200 puffs a day, a 10,000-puff device lasts about 50 days, and a 40,000-puff device lasts about 200 days, which is longer than you may want to hold one device. If you take 600 puffs a day, a 10,000-puff device lasts about 17 days and a 40,000-puff device about 67 days. Keep a rough tally for a week, and you will know which size fits.

## 2. Rechargeable or not
Many current devices have a USB-C port so you can top up the battery while the liquid is still going strong. Non-rechargeable models are lighter but can run out of battery before the liquid. Read the product page for a Type-C mention, and look at the bottom of the device for a port. See [rechargeable vs non-rechargeable disposables](/blog/rechargeable-vs-non-rechargeable-disposables/) and [how to charge a disposable](/blog/how-to-charge-a-disposable/). For large puff counts, rechargeable is nearly essential, because a sealed battery would otherwise be the limit.

## 3. Flavor family
Pick the flavor style you already enjoy: fruit, mint, dessert, tobacco or a mix. Cooling versions with "ice" in the name add a menthol-type chill. Browse the full range in [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/), and read [vape flavor profiles explained](/blog/vape-flavor-profiles-explained/) and [best disposable vapes for flavor lovers](/blog/best-disposable-vapes-for-flavor-lovers/) if you want help. If you are new, choose a familiar flavor, such as strawberry, watermelon or mint, rather than an exotic blend, so that you are judging the device, not a surprising taste.

## 4. Nicotine strength
Most disposables are sold around 5% nicotine (50 mg/mL). Check the label for the exact strength and read our [nicotine strength guide](/blog/nicotine-strength-guide/) if you are unsure. Nicotine is addictive, and a higher number is not better. Some brands offer lower strengths, and zero-nicotine options exist. Disposables use nicotine salts, which are smooth at high strength in low-power devices; see [nicotine salts vs freebase](/blog/nicotine-salts-vs-freebase/).

## 5. Screen and extras
Some devices show battery and liquid levels on a small display. It is helpful, but not essential. Other extras include adjustable airflow, power or boost modes and light effects. They add cost and sometimes complexity. See [screen vs no-screen disposables](/blog/screen-vs-no-screen-disposable-vapes/) and [adjustable airflow explained](/blog/adjustable-airflow-explained/). Choose extras that you will actually use.

## 6. Price per puff
Divide the price by the puff count to compare fairly. Bulk and multi-pack deals often lower it further. For example, a $15.99 device with 5,000 puffs costs about $3.20 per 1,000 puffs, a $17.99 device with 20,000 puffs about $0.90 and a $17.99 device with 50,000 puffs about $0.36. See [how to compare vape prices per puff](/blog/how-to-compare-vape-prices-per-puff/). A lower cost per puff is only value if you will use the puffs, so match capacity to your use first.

## 7. Where you buy
Buy from a retailer that verifies age, ships with adult signature and publishes clear [shipping](/shipping/) and refund terms. Check that packaging carries the nicotine warning, and be wary of prices far below the market; see [how to spot counterfeit vapes](/blog/how-to-spot-counterfeit-vapes/). A seller that explains its sourcing, its returns and its delivery is more likely to deal in genuine products.

## A worked example
Suppose you are choosing between three devices. Device A is a 5,000-puff, non-rechargeable device at $13.99. Device B is a 25,000-puff rechargeable device at $17.99 with a screen. Device C is a 50,000-puff rechargeable device at $18.99 without a screen. You take about 300 puffs a day. Device A lasts about 17 days at $0.84 per day. Device B lasts about 83 days at about $0.22 per day. Device C lasts about 167 days at about $0.11 per day. If you want to try a flavor, Device A is low commitment. If you want value, Device C wins, but only if you will use it for five or six months and keep the flavor interesting. Device B is a sensible middle choice. The numbers show how capacity changes cost per day.

## Handling and storage
Keep devices cool, dry and upright, away from children and pets; see [how to store disposable vapes](/blog/how-to-store-disposable-vapes/). Do not leave them in a hot car. Charge rechargeable ones on a hard surface and unplug when full, as explained in [battery care basics](/blog/lithium-battery-care-basics-for-vapes/).

## Disposal
When a device is finished, take it to a hazardous waste or electronics recycling site; see [how to dispose of vapes and batteries](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/). Do not put it in household trash.

## Common mistakes
- **Buying the biggest device** without checking whether you will use it.
- **Ignoring the charging port,** and running out of battery early.
- **Choosing an exotic flavor first.**
- **Comparing price without puff count.**
- **Buying from a seller with no policies,** or at a price that is too good to be true.
- **Leaving devices where children or pets can reach them.**

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Is a higher puff count always better?
No. It lowers cost per puff, but only helps if you will use the device, and battery and flavor matter too.

### Are all disposables the same strength?
Most are around 5%, but check the label. Some offer lower strengths.

### Can I refill a disposable?
No. Disposables are sealed. Do not open them.

### How do I know a device is genuine?
Compare packaging with the brand's official images, check the warning statement and buy from a reputable seller.

### Can I return a disposable I do not like?
Opened or used products cannot be returned. Try a smaller size or a single unit of a new flavor first. See [refund and return policy explained](/blog/refund-and-return-policy-explained/).

## Shop
Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). Our product pages list puff count, strength and pack options, and your choice updates the price. Orders of $200 or more after discount ship free, and cryptocurrency and gift cards save 10%. All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## How to read a disposable's product page
A good listing gives you the brand and model, the flavor, the puff count, the nicotine strength, the battery and charging port, any extras and the pack options. Read them in that order, and write down the numbers. If a listing hides the puff count or the strength, treat it with caution. On our pages, options such as a single device or a 5-pack appear above the Add to Cart button, and the price updates when you choose. See [how to read a vape product page](/blog/how-to-read-a-vape-product-page/) for a walkthrough.

## Three buyer profiles
### The occasional user
You take a few puffs a day, or you only vape socially. Choose a smaller device, around 5,000 to 15,000 puffs, in a flavor you know. A single unit is enough, and you avoid the risk of a large device going stale.

### The regular user
You vape through the day. Choose a rechargeable device with 25,000 puffs or more, compare cost per 1,000 puffs and consider a 5-pack of a flavor you know you like. Keep a spare, so that you are never without.

### The flavor explorer
You like variety. Buy single units of several flavors, in mid-sized devices, rather than one large device. Keep notes about what you like, and rotate flavors to avoid palate fatigue. See [best disposable vapes for flavor lovers](/blog/best-disposable-vapes-for-flavor-lovers/).

## When a cheaper device is not cheaper
A very low price per device can hide a poor cost per puff, a weak battery or a short life. A $9.99 device that gives 2,000 puffs costs $5.00 per 1,000 puffs, which is far more than a $17.99 device with 25,000 puffs at about $0.72. Always divide, and compare. Beware also of prices far below the market, which may signal counterfeit or old stock. See [how to spot counterfeit vapes](/blog/how-to-spot-counterfeit-vapes/).

## Planning an order around thresholds
Our minimum order is $100, and orders of $200 or more after discount ship free. Cryptocurrency and gift cards save 10%. If you are buying several devices, plan the cart so that it reaches $200 after discount, which needs a subtotal of about $222 if you pay by crypto or gift card. See [minimum order and free shipping explained](/blog/minimum-order-and-free-shipping-explained/) and [the 10% crypto and gift card discount](/blog/crypto-discount-how-it-works/).
